what: A rotating crank drives a coupler and a rocker through a closed four-bar linkage. Wave: three 16/48/32/48 mm four-bar linkages compare crank phase and nonlinear rocker motion. Offsets [0, 120, 240] degrees.
try: Reset and run. Compare the continuously turning crank with the rocking output.
Find the two extremes of the output and watch its changing speed between them.
For Tidal Trio, compare Wave, Together, Alternating and Reverse Wave from Reset.
why: All four link lengths constrain the loop at once. The output angle is a nonlinear function of crank angle. Tidal Trio uses 16/48/32/48 mm links and a rocker sweep near 63.07°; three crank phase offsets create a travelling pattern.
matters: Linkages turn simple rotary drives into useful repeated motions.
question: Does a 120° crank offset mean a 120° rocker offset?
answer: No. The nonlinear four-bar relation changes the rocker angle and speed throughout each cycle.
further: Compare equal crank-phase spacing with equal time spacing of rocker peaks.
Compare the nearly parallel tray of the lift.
formula: crank vector + coupler vector = fixed-pivot vector + rocker vector
